messages:
maya: noticing lots of tiny connection resets on model-serving pods in us-west2 today, ~100-200ms windows where gRPC streams drop and then recover.
jon: seen similar — CI/bench shows tiny token-time jitter across batches, looks like packet-level blips.
liam: any correlation with autoscaler churn or GPU backfills?
maya: checked node events, no recent scale events. node uptime stable. GPUs not being re-assigned.
olga: I grabbed tcpdump from one pod pair during a blip:
```
17:03:14.123456 IP pod-a > pod-b: Flags [.], ack 12345, win 502, length 0
17:03:14.124001 IP pod-a > pod-b: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12395, ack 54321, win 502, length 50
17:03:14.124450 IP pod-b > pod-a: Flags [.], ack 12395, win 512, length 0
17:03:14.223800 IP pod-a > pod-b: retransmission, seq 12395:12445, ack 54321, win 480, length 50
```
maya: you can see a ~100ms gap before retransmit. not full node path loss, just micro-bursts.
jon: are Geneve counters showing drops? I queried the encap stats on the leaf: `ip -s link show geneve0` — minor rx_errors on a few interfaces.
liam: did we see any MTU mismatches or offload toggles? those can cause single-packet fragmentation and drops.
maya: MTU matches 1450 across. gso/gro enabled. I also checked NIC offload settings, nothing changed.
olga: added a short eBPF probe to count skb->xmit failures at the kernel qdisc level, saw spikes that align with the blips.
infra-bot: deploy 2478901250 by liam — eBPF probe pushed to canary nodes. :white_check_mark:
sre-oncall: can we repro with a tight ping or iperf loop between two pods? if not reproducible, harder to triage.
jon: i ran `nping --tcp -p 50051 --rate 200` between pods. saw periodic 80-120ms spikes every ~8-12 minutes.
liam: interestingly, the bursts line up with a background kube-proxy conntrack GC job on the host (crons at minute % 10).
maya: timeline: blip at 17:03, conntrack GC at 17:02:58 on that host. we should test disabling GC window.
olga: also noticed when we move the pod pair to the same NUMA node on the host, blips reduce. suggests CPU/irq scheduling + qdisc interaction.
jon: hypothesis: conntrack/full GC + heavy qdisc processing on core => occasional skb fail/requeue causing single-packet timeouts for gRPC keepalive.
liam: short-term mitigation: 1) spread kube-proxy GC jitter, 2) pin model-serving pod interrupts to isolated cores, 3) increase gRPC keepalive timeout slightly.
maya: rolling those mitigations now on canary fleet (50 pods). will report after 2 hours.
olga: FYI I opened a support ticket with NIC vendor referencing skb requeue patterns and Geneve counters, attached captures. Ticket #NIC-8342.
sre-oncall: if canary looks good, we can roll to all us-west2 nodes and add a long-term plan: kernel qdisc tuning + test with RDMA bypass on eligible infra.
jon: adding a perf trace collection job to nightly so we get stacks when bursts occur.
maya: update: +3 hours into canary, errors down from ~12/hr -> ~1/hr, still seeing 1-2 minute microbursts but much less frequent.
liam: sounds promising. schedule a follow up postmortem if it resurfaces.
maya: thanks all — will keep thread updated. :raised_hands:
